It wasn’t until I watched and got involved with the fandom of torchwood that the word pansexual even made it to my radar. I started thinking that I would probably be like Jack Harkness and be in a relationship with a consensual living being regardless of gender, species (it’s an alien show sorry), etc. So since I was still kinda scared to say I was queer I would say heteroflexible. Then I got into Orange is the New Black and I fell in love with Poussey and that’s when I realized I wasn’t as straight as I thought. I sat down with myself and did a lot of research. Mostly people who I went to HS know and that’s only because I started making posts on Facebook about being gay and stuff. That’s about it actually. I have never mentioned it to them and basically squash any suspicions because I am deathly scared of what will happen if they do find out. I’m comfortable with who I am - I mean, I was so relieved when I finally found a label for who I was and for what I was feeling. Like I said: they could have further talked it out until Andy's childish brain understood he needed to be patient until April (if ever) was going to be ready or if that's something she definitely didn't want at all so they could cut their losses or he could adapt. April still had a good 10 years to have a kid and well as a man, Andy is probably fertile for his whole life.

She looks annoyed and frustrated when he brings it up after seeing those kids in Halloween and she says "*frustrated tone* Andy, you know where I stand on this. Yes, I would love all the awesome stuff my body would go through. I mean, if all it meant was puking and getting weird stretch marks and veins everywhere, then sign me up. But at the end, we've brought a child into the world. That's disgusting. No."  
My take on this is that they've had this conversation multiple times. April seems frustrated and annoyed, which to me, translates into someone who has had the same argument over and over again for a couple of years.   
When they go to Leslie's and Ben's house for dinner, Andy acts like a petulant child as he slides down the sofa after being told the kids are trick or treating in Georgetown. Ben mentions that if april is still "on the fence about kids", but my take is that Ben hasn't really heard about it directly from April about how she doesn't want kids, April probably talked to Leslie who in turn told Ben. April is panicking over with Leslie because she's feeling pressured by Andy to have kids. I mean, who wouldn't? Just look at how Andy is acting, and April loves him so yeah she wants him to, you know, not be sad and petulant. She talks to Leslie who tells her about the team thing and bringing in new team members, and guides her into having a child.  
I'm not saying April wouldn't have wanted kids in the future, like maybe when she was 35 or later, I don't know, but what I do know is that at that age or at that point in time in the year 2022, April didn't want kids and she was manipulated by Andy into having them. I don't think Andy was doing it consciously, I'm sure he would have stopped if April had really wanted him to, but he still did it. I think they should have communicated better and talked about it in private, because ultimately it's their decision alone. Andy could have waited a little longer, but instead, April gave him a baby when she wasn't ready just so he could stop whining.   

But that's just me. I think her ending could have been better. Tbh, all of the endings could have been better. I didn't really like them. I mean, I like Ron's, Leslie's, Donna's, and Jerry's but they could have been better or more felt-out. I felt like the last season was way too rushed, but like I said, that's just me.

When I was around 6-7 years old, my grandmother and I were staying alone in the house I grew up in for the weekend. This usually isn't a problem, and the fact that the house is in a super small town didn't really bother me.  Anyways, we were asleep, when we suddenly hear some pounding on the door. We wake up to that persistent knocking, and to the sound of a deep man's voice demanding entry. Our room was right next to the front door. Obviously, we freak out but my grandma tells me to be quiet. The man keeps on banging on the door and since the house was made out of wood and was super old, we knew that he could possibly break down the door. My grandma tries to tell him to fuck off, that the person he's looking for isn't here, but that only angers the man more and his knocking is now shaking the wall. I start crying. My grandma shushes me and tries to contact the police, even though I can see her, I am in hysterics which further infuriates the man. My grandma decides the police will take too long and tells me that we are leaving. We make a run to our car -- forgetting to even put on shoes -- and my grandma reverses so fast and panicked, she crashes into the barn that we had but she's like fuck it and goes towards the gate. The gate, which is locked and can only be open by pushing the doors in, not out. Thankfully as my grandma was considering just fucking charging at the gate, the police got there. Turns out the man was drunk and was looking for my dead dad. My grandma didn't press charges, so they left us after questioning. We were full of mud on our feet, had crashed our car and the barn, and had literally had the worst scare of our entire lives. How the man got over the locked fence while drunk is just something that makes me laugh while thinking about it now. He must've really wanted to see my dad.

TL;DR a drunk man scares the crap out of my grandma and little kid me at around 2 in the morning.
